A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ENFD does not change over time in HIV+ subjects and that the use of d4T in combination ART is not a risk factor for neuropathy.

distal leg ENDF is a useful predictor of HIV neuropathy risk in certain populations, but its use in other populations is limited by individual variation, the impact of other risk factors and the impact of antiretrovirus medications on distal leg nerve fibers.
the distal leg ENFd is a useful predictor of HIV neuropathy risk, but the ENFd is not impacted by the nucleoside backbone of ART and may not be a useful biomarker in certain populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ENFD may be a useful predictor of neuropathy risk in certain populations but not in all populations, and that it is not a reliable surrogate marker of neuropathy risk or neuropathy severity.
ENFD may be a marker of general body health and not just HIV neuropathy risk.
ENFD changes over time in HIV-infected subjects, with individual variations in the direction and magnitude of the change.
